question: What was the approximate overall growth target in India’s First Five-Year Plan?

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in 1951.
 
• The main focus of the First Five-Year Plan was on the agricultural sector, aiming to increase the output and productivity of the agricultural sector.
 
• The overall growth target set for the First Five-Year Plan was approximately 2.1% per annum.
 
• This plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which emphasized the importance of investment for economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans of India**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs, introduced by the Government of India, aimed at achieving rapid economic growth and development.
 
• They were inspired by the Soviet model of economic planning and were implemented from 1951 to 2017.
 
• Each plan had its specific objectives and priorities, addressing various sectors such as agriculture, industry, education, and health.
 
• The Planning Commission, which was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015, was responsible for formulating and monitoring these plans.
 
 
 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**
 
 
• The Harrod-Domar model is an economic growth model that suggests that the growth rate of an economy depends on the level of savings and the productivity of investment.
 
• According to this model, higher savings and investment rates lead to higher economic growth rates.
 
• The model emphasizes the role of capital accumulation in driving economic growth and development.
 
• This model was used as a theoretical foundation for the First Five-Year Plan of India.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Sector in India**
 
 
• Agriculture plays a vital role in the Indian economy, being the primary source of livelihood for a significant portion of the population.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan aimed to increase agricultural production to achieve food self-sufficiency and improve rural livelihoods.
 
• Various initiatives, such as irrigation projects, land reforms, and improved agricultural practices, were undertaken to boost agricultural productivity.
 
• Successful implementation of these initiatives resulted in substantial growth in the agricultural sector during the First Five-Year Plan.
